capabilities: Scan a designated asset folder for images without sidecar notes
Generate titles, categories, keywords, and descriptions with a local Vision-Language Model
Create markdown sidecar notes with YAML frontmatter next to each image
Extract vault-wide links and embeds of each image into a linked_notes list
Batch-process images sequentially with automatic downscaling before inference
extras: Installation is manual only (release files placed into .obsidian/plugins); the README includes a full Japanese translation, and the manifest notes the plugin has not been reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built it from an experimental Python-based image archival workflow developed to manage large-scale creative image collections inside Obsidian.
problem: Images in a vault carry no searchable metadata, and describing large image libraries by hand is impractical while cloud vision APIs raise privacy and cost concerns.

relations.evidence: Designed to work seamlessly with local LLM/VLM servers like LM Studio or Ollama
Designed to work seamlessly with local LLM/VLM servers like LM Studio or Ollama

requires.name: local OpenAI-compatible vision server (LM Studio or Ollama)
API key (dummy for local servers, real for remote services)

summary: Image asset tagger that scans a vault folder and uses a local Vision-Language Model to generate markdown sidecar notes with YAML metadata for images.
